Been with my wife for eight years. Lately things have just not been working. We separated and we're talking about divorce. We're both on the same page about all this. It seems like the divorce could be completely amicable and not have to involve lawyers.

Anyway I went to happy hour with my coworkers tonight. From 5pm to 6pm to 7pm one by one they called it a night and left. By 9pm it was just me and my coworker. Let's call her Emma for the sake of anonymity. So it's just us. Well, and some creepy dude who invited himself into our conversation. She asks me if Molly (name changed, our boss) had texted me (since my boss tends to text us after hours about work related stuff). I look at my phone and it's a chat from Emma saying we should ditch this guy. I say "oh yeah Molly texted me too." and come up with a BS story that will allow us to escape.

We head down the street to another bar. We sat there and had the most incredible conversation. It was real. We talked about our hopes, dreams, fears, etc. For some backstory, she just went through a divorce herself with a man who didn't treasure her at all and who scoffed at her dreams (to be a journalist/documentary writer). I was fascinated with her story of how her uncle is a Mayan archaeologist and how she wants to do a documentary on all these women archaeologists who studied the same area over the course of 100 years and how there is some hotel in South America which has suites named after each woman. I told her about my dream to go back to school and get a BS in computer science. She was encouraging and supportive of that dream as I was to hers. We realized that neither of our spouses (whether former or soon to be) had supported our dreams at all.

Her body language was very loud and clear to me. The dreamy look in her eyes, her playing with her straw and smiling when I talked to her, and occasional touching of each other's arm or hand. Unless I was extremely mistaken, I felt that she was into me. We match up on so many levels. I can have an intellectual conversation with her, about existentialism, politics, the future of humankind, etc.

We returned to the first bar of the night. Creepy dude was still there but he was preoccupied with other women. The barkeep/owner (a friend of both mine and Emma's) brought us drinks on the house as well as chocolate covered strawberries and some kind of Brazilian dessert that consisted of dolce de leche and coconut. We enjoyed each other's company as we dove into that delectable treat. It really felt like a date by the end of it.

I walked her to her car, gave her a warm hug, and left. I texted her, telling her to let me know when she got home (since it was late). She did.

Now I sit here, in a blissful haze comprised of traces of alcohol in my system plus the feeling that I may have met someone totally compatible and interested in me. However, I am faced with the problem that my wife and I have only just separated. Nothing is official yet. I should not be doing anything that resembles a date, despite it not actually being one.

I'm not looking for advice or anything. I just needed to tell someone because there is obviously no one I know who could tell. I should mention that the entire time we were talking about relationships and such she kept saying that I should "take my blinders off and see what I might be missing otherwise". If that isn't a very loud and clear "I WANT YOU" I don't know what is.

Devil's advocate: I completely misread her and my alcohol fueled state combined with the emotional stress I've experienced lately has created a false interest where none truly exists. If that's the case, so be it. I'm just gonna see where this goes.
I'm going through the early stages of divorce with my wife and I just had what might have been a date with a coworker.
